newsitem.title: INDIA: India orders Sobhraj deportation, bans re-entry.
newsitem.headline: India orders Sobhraj deportation, bans re-entry.

text.p: India on Monday ordered the deportation of notorious criminal Charles Sobhraj to his native France and barred him from re-entering the country again.
Sobhraj's lawyer Rajan Bakshi told reporters the country's Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO) had passed an order on Monday for his client's deportation.
"They have given a deportation order today and it is most likely to be executed tonight," Bakshi said. "He is to leave the country as soon as possible and not be allowed to come back thereafter."
"The French embassy has given his travel documents and the FRRO has already bought the ticket so there is nothing that should delay his departure any longer," Bakshi added.
Sobhraj was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He has since been charged with a long string of crimes including murder.
He has served time for some and won acquittal for others. A dramatic jailbreak in 1986 earned him fame.
Sobhraj, 52, who has spent much of the last two decades in Indian prisons, has said he would rather live in India.
"I would have loved to stay here but I don't really have a choice, I am obliged to go," Sobhraj told reporters from inside a police van outside a Delhi courtroom.

Last week French officials in Paris confirmed that Sobhraj was free to return to France, adding that Paris was prepared to provide him with a laissez-passer facilitating his return once India issued an order to expel him.
A laissez-passer is a one-way document that would allow Sobhraj to be deported to Paris. The temporary travel pass would not allow Sobhraj to enter a third country.
"I am sad and happy -- happy because I will be a free man and sad because I am leaving part of my family in India," Sobhraj said. Sobhraj has two half-sisters in India.
Asked what he was taking with him from India, he said: "I bought new clothes and some personal belongings...that's all."
Sobhraj would be set free once he was deported to France, a FRRO official said.
Sobhraj said he would like to roam the streets of Paris to enjoy his freedom. "I want to take a walk on the bank of the River Seine in Paris," he said.

He plans to concentrate on working on a $15 million English-language film based on his life, to be produced in France with American actors. He said he would write the script but would not play the title role.
Sobhraj is also considering an offer from a U.S.-based film company that had first contacted him in 1994 for a film on his prison life.

"Tristar made the offer in 1994 but we kept it pending because I was in jail. But now we want to reconsider the offer...it will be a film based on my years in jail, unlike the French production which is more autobiographical in nature," he said.
Sobhraj said he deliberately chose to break out of New Delhi's high-security Tihar Jail in 1986 to avoid extradition to Thailand, where he certainly would have faced a death penalty.
"I broke out of jail to avoid the extradition order ...I had to make a case big enough for them not to dismiss," he said.
"I was here only on a fair trial. I committed an offence and I served my sentence," he said. "I am looking forward to starting my real life and also my reel life."
